response: Yes, tailored interventions can increase mammography use among HMO women. According to the available data, telephone counseling has been found to be particularly effective in promoting change among nonadherent women, suggesting that it may be a preferred first-line intervention for getting nonadherent women on schedule for mammography screening. While tailored print communications may not be as effective, additional interventions will still be needed to maintain women's adherence to mammography.
